learningObjectives.title: Classical style and composers (Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven)

questions.q: Which dates best represent the Classical period in Western music?
questions.explain: The Classical period is conventionally dated from around 1750 to about 1820.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'Father of the Symphony' and the 'Father of the String Quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive development of both genres earned him these titles.

questions.q: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born?
questions.explain: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756.

questions.q: Which set of dates is correct for Ludwig van Beethoven?
questions.explain: Beethoven lived from 1770 to 1827.

questions.q: What are the three main sections of sonata form, in order?
questions.explain: Sonata form is built from an exposition, a development and a recapitulation.

questions.q: Which instruments make up a standard string quartet?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet consists of first violin, second violin, viola and cello.

questions.q: How many movements does a typical Classical symphony have?
questions.explain: A standard Classical symphony has four movements.

questions.q: What is an 'Alberti bass'?
options: A broken-chord accompaniment pattern in the left hand
A sustained pedal note in the bass
questions.explain: An Alberti bass breaks a chord into a repeated low-high-middle-high accompanying figure.

questions.q: In the exposition of a sonata-form movement in a major key, in what key does the second subject usually appear?
questions.explain: In a major-key exposition the second subject typically moves to the dominant.

questions.q: What most characterises the development section of sonata form?
options: Both subjects are stated for the first time in the tonic
Themes are fragmented and taken through a range of different keys
A completely new melody replaces the earlier material
The music stays firmly in the home key throughout
questions.explain: The development explores and fragments earlier material while modulating widely.

questions.q: What key relationship marks the recapitulation of a sonata-form movement?
options: Both subjects now appear in the tonic key
The second subject stays in the dominant
Both subjects appear in the relative minor
The material is heard in the subdominant
questions.explain: In the recapitulation both subjects return, now resolved into the tonic key.

questions.q: Which texture is most typical of Classical music?
questions.explain: Classical music favours a clear homophonic texture of melody plus accompaniment.

questions.q: Classical melodies are often described as 'periodic'. What does this mean?
options: They use balanced phrases, such as a question (antecedent) answered by a response (consequent)
They avoid any sense of regular phrasing
They are always played in unison
They consist of long, unbroken chromatic lines
questions.explain: Periodic phrasing balances an antecedent phrase with a matching consequent phrase.

questions.q: Compared with the Baroque period, the Classical style is generally noted for its:
options: Clarity, balance and largely homophonic textures
Use of the basso continuo throughout
Free, improvised ornamentation with no clear phrasing
questions.explain: Classical style prizes clarity, balance and homophony over Baroque contrapuntal density.

questions.q: The third movement of a typical Classical symphony is usually a minuet and trio. What is its overall structure?
questions.explain: The minuet is followed by a contrasting trio and then a repeat of the minuet, giving ABA.

questions.q: Why is Beethoven often seen as a transitional figure in music history?
options: He bridged the Classical and Romantic periods, expanding forms and expression
He composed entirely in the Baroque style
He wrote only operas and no instrumental music
He rejected the symphony and string quartet
questions.explain: Beethoven built on Classical forms while pushing towards the greater expression of Romanticism.

questions.q: A sonata-form movement is in C major. In which key is the second subject of the exposition most likely to be heard?
questions.explain: The dominant of C major is G major, the usual key for the second subject.

questions.q: A pianist plays a clear tune in the right hand while the left hand repeats the pattern C-G-E-G, C-G-E-G. Which features are demonstrated?
options: Homophonic texture with an Alberti bass accompaniment
A monophonic melody with no accompaniment
questions.explain: A single melody over a broken-chord left hand is homophony using an Alberti bass.

questions.q: In a movement you hear the opening themes broken into short fragments and passed rapidly through several unrelated keys. Which section are you most likely hearing?
questions.explain: Fragmenting themes and modulating through many keys is characteristic of the development.

questions.q: A Classical melody presents a four-bar phrase that sounds like an unfinished 'question', immediately answered by a four-bar phrase that sounds 'finished'. This is an example of:
questions.explain: A questioning antecedent answered by a resolving consequent is balanced periodic phrasing.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Music (0410) syllabus; Area of Study 2: Classical Music
